fullPassage:
When my friend Dan suggested we travel to San Francisco and Yosemite, I was thrilled but also nervous. As a wheelchair user, I wasn’t sure how easy it would be to get around. But Dan assured me that we’d figure it out together. So I gathered my courage and agreed to go.

On the first day in San Francisco, we wanted to ride the famous cable cars. Unfortunately, they don’t accommodate wheelchairs. We were disappointed at first, but we quickly found an alternative — a tour bus with wheelchair access. The bus took us around the city, and we stopped at Fisherman’s Wharf, where we watched sea lions sunbathing on the docks. Later, we took a cruise that passed under the Golden Gate Bridge. Watching the sunset from the water was absolutely breathtaking.

Yosemite National Park is about four hours from San Francisco. It is five times bigger than Seoul, with grand waterfalls, deep valleys, and thick forests. Dan’s Uncle Roy drove us there. One of the first things we saw were the giant sequoias. The most impressive one was the Grizzly Giant, which stands 63.7 meters tall and is about 3,000 years old. While exploring the park, we even encountered a black bear in the distance!

The next morning, I tried a hand-crank bike on a paved trail. It was my first time, and I felt a rush of freedom as I moved through the park on my own. Later, we visited Tunnel View, one of the most famous viewpoints in Yosemite. The view of the valley below was beyond words. We ended the day by the Merced River, listening to the gentle sound of the water.

This trip taught me that obstacles don’t have to stop you. With courage and the support of good friends, you can go further than you ever imagined. I’m already looking forward to my next adventure.

Naadam is a traditional festival held every July in Mongolia. It features three main sports: wrestling, archery, and horse racing. These events have been part of Mongolian culture for centuries and attract both locals and tourists from around the world.

Día de los Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a Mexican celebration honoring deceased loved ones. Families build altars, decorate graves, and share food and stories to remember those who have passed away. It is celebrated on November 1st and 2nd each year.

Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year’s celebration. One of its most well-known traditions is first footing, where the first person to enter a home after midnight is believed to bring good luck for the coming year.

questions.passage: On the first day in San Francisco, we wanted to ride the famous cable cars. Unfortunately, they don’t accommodate wheelchairs. We were disappointed at first, but we quickly found an alternative — a tour bus with wheelchair access. The bus took us around the city, and we stopped at Fisherman’s Wharf, __________ we watched sea lions sunbathing on the docks.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 Fisherman’s Wharf(장소)를 수식하며 뒤에 완전한 절(we watched ...)이 오므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ where: 장소 선행사(Fisherman’s Wharf) + 완전한 절 → 관계부사
❌ ① which: 관계대명사 → 뒤에 불완전한 절 필요
❌ ② what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사가 있으므로 불가
❌ ④ when: 시간 관계부사 → 장소 선행사와 불일치
det.tip: 장소 선행사 + where + 완전한 절: 장소를 수식하는 관계부사

questions.passage: Later, we took a cruise that passed under the Golden Gate Bridge. Watching the sunset from the water was absolutely __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주어(Watching the sunset)가 감동을 유발하는 대상이므로 현재분사형 형용사 breathtaking이 적절하다. "숨이 멎을 만큼 아름다운"
det.analysis:
✅ ② breathtaking: 감정 유발 주체 → -ing형 형용사
❌ ① breathtaken: 존재하지 않는 형태
❌ ③ breathtook: 과거형 동사 → 보어 자리에 부적절
❌ ④ to breathtake: to부정사 → 보어 자리에 부적절
det.tip: 감정 형용사: 사물/상황 주어 → -ing (breathtaking, amazing) | 사람 주어 → -ed

questions.passage: One of the first things we saw were the giant sequoias. The most impressive one was the Grizzly Giant, __________ stands 63.7 meters tall and is about 3,000 years old.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 the Grizzly Giant(사물)를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 계속적 용법으로 추가 정보를 제공한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① which: 사물 선행사(the Grizzly Giant) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ② who: 사람 선행사용 → 나무는 사물
❌ ③ what: 선행사 포함 → 앞에 선행사가 이미 있음
❌ ④ where: 관계부사 → 뒤에 주어(stands의 주어) 필요
det.tip: 사물 선행사 + , which + 동사: 계속적 용법의 관계대명사

questions.passage: When my friend Dan suggested we travel to San Francisco and Yosemite, I was ①<u>thrilled</u> but also nervous. As a wheelchair user, I wasn’t sure how easy it would be to get around. But Dan ②<u>was assured</u> me that we’d figure it out together. So I gathered my courage and ③<u>agreed</u> to go.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② was assured → assured: Dan이 나에게 확신시켜준 것(능동)이므로 능동태 assured가 적절하다. "Dan assured me that ~" = Dan이 나를 안심시켰다
det.analysis:
❌ ② was assured(수동) → assured(능동): Dan이 주어이고 me가 목적어이므로 능동태
✅ ① thrilled: 감정을 느끼는 주어(I) → 과거분사 형용사 올바름
✅ ③ agreed: 과거형 동사 → "동의했다" 올바름
det.tip: assure + 목적어 + that절: ~에게 확신시키다 (능동) / be assured that: ~을 확신하다 (수동 - 주어가 확신을 받는 쪽)

questions.passage: The next morning, I tried a hand-crank bike on a paved trail. It was my first time, and I felt a rush of freedom as I ①<u>moved</u> through the park on my own. Later, we visited Tunnel View, one of the most famous viewpoints in Yosemite. The view of the valley below was ②<u>beyond</u> words. We ended the day by the Merced River, ③<u>listened</u> to the gentle sound of the water.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ listened → listening: 주절(We ended the day)과 동시에 일어나는 부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문이므로 현재분사 listening이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ listened(과거형) → listening(현재분사): 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가 → 분사구문
✅ ① moved: 과거형 동사 → "이동했다" 올바름
✅ ② beyond: 전치사 → "말로 표현할 수 없는" 올바름
det.tip: 분사구문 (동시동작): 주절, ~ing ... → 접속사 없이 두 동작을 연결

questions.passage: On the first day in San Francisco, we wanted to ride the famous cable cars. Unfortunately, they don’t accommodate wheelchairs. We were disappointed at first, but we quickly found an alternative — a tour bus with wheelchair access. The bus took us around the city, and we stopped at Fisherman’s Wharf, where we watched sea lions sunbathing on the docks. Later, we took a cruise that passed under the Golden Gate Bridge. Watching the sunset from the water was absolutely breathtaking.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "we quickly found an alternative — a tour bus with wheelchair access. The bus took us around the city" → 투어 버스를 타고 도시를 돌아다녔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 투어 버스로 도시를 돌아다님: 본문과 일치
❌ ① 케이블카는 휠체어를 수용하지 않아 타지 못함
❌ ③ sea lions(바다사자)를 봄, 돌고래(dolphins)가 아님
❌ ④ 크루즈로 다리 아래를 지남, 걸어서 건넌 것이 아님
det.tip: 내용 일치: 선택지의 세부 단어(케이블카 vs 버스, 바다사자 vs 돌고래)를 정확히 대조

ch: 필자와 Dan은 투어 버스를 타고 도시를 돌아다녔다.
Golden Gate Bridge 위를 걸어서 건넜다.

questions.passage: Yosemite National Park is about four hours from San Francisco. It is five times bigger than Seoul, with grand waterfalls, deep valleys, and thick forests. Dan’s Uncle Roy drove us there. One of the first things we saw were the giant sequoias. The most impressive one was the Grizzly Giant, which stands 63.7 meters tall and is about 3,000 years old. While exploring the park, we even encountered a black bear in the distance!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "the Grizzly Giant, which stands 63.7 meters tall" → 63.7미터인데, 선택지에서 36.7미터라고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 36.7미터 → 본문은 63.7미터 (숫자 오류)
✅ ① "about four hours from San Francisco" → 일치
✅ ② "five times bigger than Seoul" → 일치
✅ ④ "Uncle Roy drove us there" → 일치
det.tip: 숫자/수치를 묻는 불일치 문제: 본문의 정확한 숫자를 확인 (63.7 vs 36.7)

questions.passage: This trip taught me that obstacles don’t have to stop you. With courage and the support of good friends, you can go further than you ever imagined. I’m already looking forward to my next adventure.
questions.stem: 이 글(여행기) 전체의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "obstacles don’t have to stop you. With courage and the support of good friends, you can go further than you ever imagined" → 장애를 극복하고 여행으로 얻은 용기와 교훈
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 장애 극복 + 용기 + 교훈: "obstacles don’t have to stop you" + "courage and the support of good friends"
❌ ① 관광지 소개는 부분적 내용일 뿐 주제 아님
❌ ② 동식물 생태계는 주제가 아님
❌ ④ 여행 가이드가 아닌 개인 여행기
❌ ⑤ 우정의 시작 계기는 언급되지 않음
det.tip: 여행기의 주제: 결론부에서 필자가 깨달은 핵심 교훈을 찾기

ch: 장애를 극복하고 여행을 통해 얻은 용기와 교훈

questions.passage: On the first day in San Francisco, we wanted to ride the famous cable cars. Unfortunately, they don’t accommodate wheelchairs. We were disappointed at first, but we quickly found __________ — a tour bus with wheelchair access.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 케이블카를 탈 수 없어 실망했지만 빠르게 대안(an alternative)을 찾았다 — 휠체어 접근이 가능한 투어 버스.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ an alternative: 빈칸 뒤 대시 이후 "a tour bus"가 그 대안의 구체적 내용
❌ ① disappointment: 실망은 이미 느낀 감정이고 "found"의 목적어로 부적절
❌ ② fear: 두려움을 찾았다는 문맥과 불일치
❌ ④ a refund: 환불은 문맥과 무관
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤의 대시(—)나 콤마 뒤 부연 설명이 빈칸의 핵심 단서

questions.passage: The next morning, I tried a hand-crank bike on a paved trail. It was my first time, and I felt __________ as I moved through the park on my own.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 처음으로 핸드 크랭크 자전거를 타고 스스로 공원을 이동하면서 자유의 전율(a rush of freedom)을 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① a rush of freedom: "on my own"(스스로) + 처음 시도 + 공원 이동 → 자유로움
❌ ② a sense of danger: 위험 감각은 긍정적 문맥과 불일치
❌ ③ a wave of regret: 후회는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ a moment of confusion: 혼란은 문맥과 무관
det.tip: "on my own"(혼자 힘으로)이 핵심 단서 → 휠체어 사용자가 스스로 이동한 감정

questions.passage: This trip taught me that __________ don’t have to stop you. With __________ and the support of good friends, you can go further than you ever imagined. I’m already looking forward to my next adventure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 두 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 수 없는 것은?

det.korean: 첫 번째 빈칸: "____은 당신을 멈추게 할 필요가 없다" → obstacles(장애물). 두 번째 빈칸: "__와 좋은 친구의 지지로" → courage(용기). courage는 첫 번째 빈칸에 들어가면 "용기가 당신을 멈추게 할 필요가 없다"가 되어 문맥과 맞지 않는다. 따라서 공통으로 들어갈 수 없는 것은 없지만, 문제는 각 빈칸에 각각 다른 단어가 들어가는 구조. courage는 첫 빈칸에 부적절하므로 공통으로 들어갈 수 없다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② courage: 첫 빈칸 "courage don’t have to stop you"는 의미상 부자연스러움
✅ ① obstacles: 첫 빈칸에 적합 (장애물이 멈추게 할 필요 없다)
✅ ③ competition: 두 빈칸 모두 의미상 부자연스러움
✅ ④ luck: 두 빈칸 모두 의미상 부자연스러움
det.tip: "공통으로 들어갈 수 없는 것" 유형: 각 빈칸에 하나씩 넣어보고 문맥 확인

questions.passage: On the first day in San Francisco, we wanted to ride the famous cable cars. Unfortunately, they don’t accommodate wheelchairs. We were __________ (disappoint) at first, but we quickly found an alternative — a tour bus with wheelchair access.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: disappoint(동사) → disappointed(형용사): "We were + 형용사" 구문에서 사람(We)이 실망을 느끼는 쪽이므로 과거분사형 형용사
det.analysis:
disappoint(동사) → disappointed(형용사)
We were ______: 주어가 사람(We) → 감정을 느끼는 쪽 → -ed형
-ed형(disappointed): 사람이 감정을 느끼는 | -ing형(disappointing): 대상이 감정을 유발하는
det.tip: 감정 동사의 분사형: 사람 주어 → -ed (disappointed, excited) / 사물 주어 → -ing

questions.passage: One of the first things we saw were the giant sequoias. The most __________ (impress) one was the Grizzly Giant, which stands 63.7 meters tall and is about 3,000 years old.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: impress(동사) → impressive(형용사): "The most + 형용사 + 명사" 구문에서 최상급을 이루는 형용사가 필요. "가장 인상적인"
det.analysis:
impress(동사) → impressive(형용사)
"The most ______ one" → 최상급 형용사 필요
impressive = 인상적인, 감명 깊은
det.tip: impress → impressive / express → expressive — 동사 → -ive 형용사 변환

questions.passage: On the first day in San Francisco, we wanted to ride the famous cable cars. Unfortunately, they don’t accommodate wheelchairs. We were disappointed at first, but we quickly found an alternative — a tour bus with wheelchair access. The bus took us around the city, and we stopped at Fisherman’s Wharf, where we watched sea lions sunbathing on the docks. Later, we took a cruise that passed under the Golden Gate Bridge. Watching the sunset from the water was absolutely breathtaking.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 Fisherman’s Wharf에서 부두 위에서 일광욕하는 것을 본 동물을 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "we watched sea lions sunbathing on the docks" → 부두에서 일광욕하는 바다사자 = sea lions
det.analysis:
Fisherman’s Wharf에서 본 동물 = sea lions
sunbathing on the docks = 부두에서 일광욕하는
det.tip: "본문에서 찾기" 유형: 한글 힌트의 키워드(일광욕, 부두)와 대응하는 영어 표현을 정확히 찾기

questions.passage: This trip taught me that obstacles don’t have to stop you. With courage and the support of good friends, you can go further than you ever imagined. I’m already looking forward to my next adventure.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 "당신을 멈추게 할 필요가 없다"고 한 대상을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "This trip taught me that obstacles don’t have to stop you." → 장애물 = obstacles
det.analysis:
obstacles don’t have to stop you = 장애물이 당신을 멈추게 할 필요가 없다
여행을 통해 얻은 핵심 교훈
det.tip: 결론부에서 필자의 깨달음을 나타내는 핵심 단어 찾기

questions.passage: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year’s celebration. One of its most well-known traditions is first footing, where the first person to enter a home after midnight is believed to bring good luck for the coming year.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Hogmanay의 가장 잘 알려진 전통으로, 자정 이후 집에 처음 들어오는 사람이 행운을 가져온다고 믿는 풍습을 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "One of its most well-known traditions is first footing, where the first person to enter a home after midnight is believed to bring good luck" → first footing
det.analysis:
Hogmanay의 가장 잘 알려진 전통 = first footing
자정 이후 첫 방문자가 행운을 가져온다는 풍습
det.tip: Read Culture 지문에서 고유한 문화 용어를 정확히 찾기

questions.passage: When my friend Dan suggested we travel to San Francisco and Yosemite, I was thrilled but also nervous. As a wheelchair user, I wasn’t sure how easy it would be to get around. But Dan assured me that we’d figure it out together. So I gathered my courage and agreed to go.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The narrator was both excited and nervous about the trip."

det.korean: "I was thrilled but also nervous" → 필자는 설레면서도 긴장했다 → excited(=thrilled)와 nervous 모두 일치 → True
det.analysis:
✅ True: "thrilled but also nervous" = "excited and nervous" → 동일한 의미
thrilled = excited (유의어)
det.tip: 유의어 대응: thrilled = excited, nervous = anxious

The bus took us around the city, and we stopped at Fisherman’s Wharf, where we watched sea lions sunbathing on the docks. Later, we took a cruise that passed under the Golden Gate Bridge. questions.stem:
